facts.text: Flint is the county seat of Genesee County and sits along the Flint River.
Flint traces its start to a trading post that fur trader Jacob Smith founded at the Grand Traverse of the Flint River in 1819, and it incorporated in 1855.
Downtown Flint's business district is centered on Saginaw Street, just south of the Flint River.
In a project that broke ground in April 2023, the City of Flint picked up and relaid Saginaw Street's original 1898 bricks from Court Street to the Flint River.
Riverbank Park, designed by landscape architect Lawrence Halprin and completed in the early 1980s, sits on the banks of the Flint River in downtown Flint.
Carriage Town and the Grand Traverse Street District, on opposite sides of the Flint River just west of downtown, are home to many well-preserved Victorian homes.
The Flint Cultural Center campus includes the Flint Institute of Arts, Sloan Museum, the Flint Public Library, Longway Planetarium and Whiting Auditorium.

Flint's East Side is home to Applewood Estate, Mott Community College, the Cultural Center and the East Village neighborhood, and the surrounding area is known as the College and Cultural Neighborhood.

The Flint Cultural Center holds a free Holiday Walk each December; the 40th annual walk in 2025 opened with a holiday tree lighting ceremony and included live music, carolers and visits with Santa at The Whiting.

Good lighting here takes its cues from the buildings themselves.

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Flint, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Christmas light installation in Flint, MI. Rooflines, tree wraps and shrubs, designed, installed, serviced and taken down for you. Get a free estimate.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Flint, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Clean rooflines, wrapped trees and lit shrubs for Flint homes, designed and installed for you, looked after through the season and removed when it ends.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Flint's older neighborhoods are where careful installation shows. Carriage Town and the Grand Traverse Street District hold many well-preserved Victorian homes, and houses of that era tend to have steep pitches, layered trim and more corners than a newer build. Lighting them well means planning every run before anyone climbs, so the lines follow the architecture instead of fighting it. Every attachment point is chosen with the trim in mind, and the tallest trees get a plan of their own. Across the rest of the city the approach holds: we study how the house reads from the street, then design roofline, tree and shrub lighting to match. Design, installation, in-season service and takedown are all part of the job.
considerations: Gables, dormers and decorative trim look striking when lit, but only if the layout is worked out first. We map where each run starts and ends so corners stay crisp and the house reads as one clean design from the sidewalk, not a collection of separate strands.
Height is a job for the truck

Wrapping a tall trunk and its upper limbs takes more time and reach than a roofline. Our bucket-truck equipped crews handle that elevated work, which makes full tree wraps and canopy lighting realistic options for a Flint yard instead of a stretch.
Plan ahead of the Holiday Walk

The Cultural Center on the East Side hosts a free Holiday Walk each December, and the 2025 walk opened with a tree lighting. If you want the house glowing by then, start early. Installs commonly run from October into early December, and booking sooner leaves more dates to choose from.
faq: Do you install Christmas lights throughout Flint?

Yes. Flint is part of our Genesee County service area, from the historic neighborhoods west of downtown to the East Side and beyond. Call (248) 756-8915 or request a free estimate with your address, and we will talk through what your home needs.
What does the free estimate cover?

It lays out the design for your home, the areas to be lit, such as the roofline, trees and shrubs, and what is included from installation through in-season service and takedown. Everything is written down before any work is scheduled, so you can compare options and decide at your own pace.
How do you handle an older Victorian home?

Carefully, and with a plan. We study the rooflines, gables and trim before installing, choose attachment points suited to the material and keep the runs tidy at every corner. Homes like those in Carriage Town and the Grand Traverse Street District have detail that deserves that attention.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Flint, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Commercial holiday lighting in Flint, MI for downtown storefronts, offices and managed properties. Design, install, service and takedown. Free estimates.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Flint, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Lit facades, tree wraps, bistro strings and entrances for Flint businesses and property managers, with bucket-truck crews for the high work.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Downtown Flint's business district is centered on Saginaw Street, just south of the river, and the street itself sets the tone. The city relaid its original 1898 bricks from Court Street to the Flint River, and warm light against brick and older facades is holiday lighting at its most inviting. For a storefront, that can mean outlined windows and rooflines, wrapped trees on the property and bistro strings where the space allows. For offices and managed buildings elsewhere in the city, it usually means strong building outlines and a lit entrance that is easy to find on a dark December evening. We handle the height, service the display through the season and take it down when the holidays are over.
considerations: Saginaw Street is a working business district, so installation has to respect shop hours, deliveries and foot traffic. We plan the work around your schedule and the building's access points, and lift work is arranged with your entrances and sidewalks in mind.

Property managers often need one plan that covers several buildings or tenants. We can design a consistent look for the whole property and put the full scope in a single estimate, so there is one plan to approve instead of a separate conversation for every storefront.
Lighting that reads from the street

Commercial displays are seen at driving speed and from across the road, not just up close. Strong outlines, lit entrances and tree wraps that hold their shape at a distance make a property look finished to everyone passing, which is the point of lighting it at all.
faq: Do you light storefronts in downtown Flint?

Yes. Downtown storefronts, offices and managed properties across Flint are all within our service area. Tell us about the building, its frontage and what you want people to notice, and we will prepare a free estimate covering design, installation, in-season service and takedown.
Can you work with the building owner or property manager instead of the tenant?

Yes. Many commercial projects are approved by an owner, a property manager or an association rather than the business out front. We work with whoever signs off, and the estimate spells out what is included so every party sees the same scope.
When should a Flint business book commercial lighting?

Earlier than most expect. The install season runs from October into early December, and projects with lift work or several buildings take more planning. Reaching out early gives you more date options and more room to refine the design before installation.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Christmas Lights in Flint, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Permanent Christmas lights for Flint homes, app-controlled on the roofline. Set them for holidays, game days or a warm everyday glow. Get a free estimate.
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: Roofline lighting that stays up year-round and changes from your phone, for Christmas, game days, Halloween or a quiet warm-white evening.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: Permanent lighting is installed along your roofline once and controlled from an app, so the holidays no longer start with a ladder. In December it can glow warm white or run the colors of the season. The rest of the year it works as accent lighting, marks a birthday or shows team colors on game day. On a Victorian home, like the many preserved in Carriage Town and the Grand Traverse Street District, layout matters most. We plan the run so it follows the gables and trim instead of cutting across them, and so the house keeps its character in daylight. On simpler rooflines elsewhere in Flint, the same system gives the home a clean, finished outline every night of the year.
considerations: Victorian homes tend to have more angles and trim detail than a modern roofline. We plan placement so the lighting follows the house's lines and stays as unobtrusive as possible when it is off, which matters on a home whose character is the whole appeal.

The same roofline covers Christmas, the Fourth of July, Halloween and ordinary weeknights. You change colors and scenes from the app, so the house can go full holiday in December and simply look well lit for the rest of the year.
When seasonal lights still make sense

If you like a new look every year, or only decorate for a few weeks, seasonal installation may suit you better. Ask about both when you request your free estimate, and we will walk through how each would look and work on your home.
faq: Is permanent lighting available in Flint?

Yes. Permanent, app-controlled roofline lighting is available throughout Flint and the rest of our Genesee County service area. Request a free estimate or call (248) 756-8915, and we will look at your roofline and talk through where the lighting would run.
What can I use permanent lighting for besides Christmas?

Almost any night of the year. Set it for Halloween or the Fourth of July, run team colors on game days, mark a birthday, or leave it on a soft warm white as everyday accent lighting. Every change happens in the app, with no ladder involved.
Will it look right on a Victorian house?

It can look excellent, as long as the layout respects the architecture. We plan the runs around gables, peaks and trim so the lighting reads as part of the house. Your estimate describes where the lighting will go, so you can judge the fit before anything is installed.
